```{r}
# derived dataframes can be consulted in the data management file.
#' dataframe for main all analyses
hospitalization_main_df_nb <- gcs_get_object(
  "MSM_Hospitalizations/hospitalization_main_df.rds",
  bucket = "",
  parseFunction = gcs_parse_rds)

# df for sensitivity analyses of merging admissions ocurred on the same day
hospitalizations_merged_same_day_df <- gcs_get_object(
  "MSM_Hospitalizations/admissions_sensit_same_day_full.rds",
  bucket = "",
  parseFunction = gcs_parse_rds)

# df for sensitivity analyses of merging admissions ocurred on the next day

  bucket = "",
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-outcome-derivation-plot
#| fig-cap: "Illustration of 30-day readmissions derivation for a patient with four hospital admissions during the entire follow-up period (from day 1 to day 80). The patient had an index discharge on day 39 (i.e., first admission event) and then experienced subsequent hospital admissions on days 44, 54, and 69, respectively. According to the followed definition, all subsequent admissions are counted (n = 3) for the given index admission as they fall within the same 30-day window. Following this 30-day window, any subsequent hospital admission is considered a  new (second) index admission with its respective 30-day windows initiate."
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: 100%

fig_outcome_derivation <- hospitalization_main_df_nb %>%
  dplyr::select(
    patient_uuid,
    admission_age_days_firstDate,
    admission_age_days_lastDate,
    readmission,
    first_record_age_days,
    last_record_age_days
  ) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Filter for a specific patient with 3 subsequent admissions within 30 days
  filter(patient_uuid == "patient_id_number") %>%
  # Filter out admissions which are not index or 30-day UHRs
  filter(!is.na(readmission)) %>%
  mutate(
    patient_label = "Patient example",
    followup_duration = last_record_age_days - first_record_age_days
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Identify last index discharge
    last_index_discharge = if_else(readmission == "index", 
                                   admission_age_days_lastDate, NA_real_),
    last_index_discharge = zoo::na.locf(last_index_discharge, na.rm = FALSE),
    time_diff = admission_age_days_firstDate - last_index_discharge
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    readmission_label = case_when(
      readmission == "index" ~ "Index discharge day",
      str_detect(readmission, "30_days_uhr") ~ "30-day UHRs",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot(.) +
  scale_alpha_manual(name = "", values = 1) +
  geom_linerange(
    aes(y = patient_label, xmin = 1, xmax = 80),
    linetype = "dashed",
    size = .2,
  ) +

  # Add horizontal line to refer to the 30-window after index discharge
  geom_segment(aes(x = 39, xend = 69, y = 1.05, yend = 1.05),
    color = "black", size = 0.2
  ) +

  # Add left arrow at x = 39
  geom_segment(aes(x = 39, xend = 36, y = 1.05, yend = 1.05),
    color = "black", size = 0.2,
    arrow = arrow(type = "closed", length = unit(0.2, "cm"))
  ) +

  # Add right arrow at x = 69
  geom_segment(aes(x = 66, xend = 69, y = 1.05, yend = 1.05),
    color = "black", size = 0.2,
    arrow = arrow(type = "closed", length = unit(0.2, "cm"))
  ) +

  # Add label above the line
  annotate("text",
    x = 52, y = 1.1, label = "30-day window after index discharge (day 39)",
    size = 3
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(
      x = admission_age_days_firstDate,
      y = patient_label,
      colour = factor(readmission_label)
    ),
    shape = 18,
    size = 5,
    show.legend = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      x = admission_age_days_firstDate,
      y = patient_label,
      label = case_when(readmission_label == "30-day UHRs" ~ as.character(paste0(
        "day ", abs(admission_age_days_firstDate)
      )))
    ),
    size = 2.7,
    hjust = 0.5,
    vjust = -1,
    nudge_y = -0.08
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Index discharge day" = "red",
      "30-day UHRs" = "blue"
    ),
    labels = c(
      "Index discharge day" = "Index admission",
      "30-day UHRs" = "30-day UHRs"
    ),
    name = "Hospitalization type"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 80, 5),
    limits = c(0, 80)
  ) +
  labs(x = "Follow-up time (days)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7, face = "bold", margin = margin(r = -18)),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9)
  )

fig_outcome_derivation
```

# Descriptive analysis

```{r}
#| label: readmissions-data-selection
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

# Select, order and rename variables for readmission df
#' Note: readmission variable used to filter the desired subset of data
#' was derived in the data management file
readmissions_df <- hospitalization_main_df_nb %>%
  #' keep index with valid exptime and remove those with invalid index 
  #' admission which doens't allow to count readmissions (i.e. exptime == 0)
  #' Index derived in the data management file already excludes planned, birth
  #'  and outpatient admissions
  filter(readmission == "index" & !is.na(count_readmissions)) %>%
  # order, rename and select variables of interest
  dplyr::select(
    # patient identifier
    patient_uuid,
    # admissions related features
    admission_age_days_firstDate,
    admission_age_days_lastDate,
    # demographics
    sex,
    age_index_admission_yr = age_admission_yr,
    # genetic mutations
    other_epilepsy_mutations,
    recurrent_variant,
    neonatal_onset,
    # clinical history
    seizure_related_index_admission = seizure_related_admission,
    length_of_index_stay_days_cat = length_of_stay_days_cat,
    respiratory_support_index_admission = respiratory_support_admission,
    tech_assistance_ever,
    count_readmissions,
    exptime,
    # treatment history
    vns_insertion_ever,
    n_distinct_asm_index_admission = n_distinct_asm_admission,
    adverse_effect_index_admission = adverse_effect_admission,
    ketogenic_diet_admission,
    quinidine_admission
    )
```

## Distribution of 30-day UHRs per patient

### Proportion of patients with at least one index admission and one 30-day UHR

```{r}
#| label: tbl-descriptive-proportions-30-day-endpoint
#| tbl-cap: "Proportion of patients with at least one index admission and with at least one 30-day UHRs over total follow-up period"
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'

# percentage of patients with at least one 30-day UHR event
uhr_proportions <- readmissions_df %>%
  summarise(
    total_rwd_source_patients = 50,
    total_patients_with_index = n_distinct(patient_uuid),
    prop_with_index = round(total_patients_with_index / total_rwd_source_patients * 100, 1),
    total_patients_with_uhr = n_distinct(patient_uuid[which(count_readmissions >= 1)]),
    prop_with_uhr = round(total_patients_with_uhr / total_patients_with_index * 100, 1)
  ) 

uhr_prop_summary_table <- tibble(
  Statistic = c(
    "At least one index admission¹", 
    "At least one 30-day UHR²"
  ),
  'N patients (%)' = c(
    sprintf("%d (%.1f)", round(uhr_proportions$total_patients_with_index, 1), round(uhr_proportions$prop_with_index, 1)),
    sprintf("%d (%.1f)", round(uhr_proportions$total_patients_with_uhr, 1), round(uhr_proportions$prop_with_uhr, 1))
  )
)

uhr_prop_summary_table %>%
  flextable::regulartable() %>%
  flextable::autofit() %>%
  flextable::bold(part = "header", bold = TRUE) %>%  
  flextable::add_footer_lines(
    values = c(
      "¹ Percentage relative to total rwd_source patients (N = 50).",
      "² Percentage relative to patients with at least one index admission (N = 48).",
      "Note: For patients without index admissions. a) patient with only a single hospital admission, which was not classified as an index admission because the discharge date coincided with the last day of follow-up. This left no post-discharge time at risk for a 30-day UHR; b) patient without hospitalization events (loss to follow-up at day 196)."
    )
  )  %>%
  flextable::font(part = "all", fontname = "Century Gothic") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "all", size = 11) %>%
  flextable::italic(part = "footer", italic = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::align(part = "footer", align = "left") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "footer", size = 9) 
```

### Number of UHRs

```{r}
#| label: tbl-descriptive-number-per-patient-30-day-endpoint
#| tbl-cap: "Number of 30-day UHRs per patient over follow-up period"
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'

# total 30-day UHRs for each patient over follow up
uhr_by_patient <- readmissions_df %>%
  group_by(patient_uuid) %>%
  summarise(
    # sum of 30-day UHRs per patient during follow-up
    patient_readmissions = sum(count_readmissions, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# summary across patients
uhr_by_across_patient <- uhr_by_patient %>%
  summarise(
    # mean (average) number of UHRs per patient
    mean_uhr = mean(patient_readmissions, na.rm = TRUE),
    # standard deviation of UHRs per patient
    sd_uhr = sd(patient_readmissions),
    # median (50th percentile) number of UHRs per patient
    median_uhr = median(patient_readmissions),
    # minimum number of UHRs observed
    min_uhr = min(patient_readmissions),
    # maximum number of UHRs observed
    max_uhr = max(patient_readmissions),
    # 25th percentile (Q1) of UHRs per patient
    q25_uhr = quantile(patient_readmissions, 0.25),
    # 75th percentile (Q3) of UHRs per patient
    q75_uhr = quantile(patient_readmissions, 0.75)
  )

uhr_summary_table <- tibble(
  'Summary statistic' = c(
    "Mean UHRs (SD)",
    "Median UHRs (Q1–Q3)",
    "Range UHRs (min–max)"
  ),
  '30-day UHRs per patient' = c(
    sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", uhr_by_across_patient$mean_uhr, uhr_by_across_patient$sd_uhr),
    sprintf("%.1f (%.1f–%.1f)", uhr_by_across_patient$median_uhr, uhr_by_across_patient$q25_uhr, uhr_by_across_patient$q75_uhr),
    sprintf("%.1f–%.1f", uhr_by_across_patient$min_uhr, uhr_by_across_patient$max_uhr)
  )
)

uhr_summary_table %>%
  flextable::regulartable() %>%
  flextable::autofit() %>% 
  flextable::bold(part = "header", bold = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::add_footer_lines(
    values = c(
      "Note 1: average follow-up time: 5.4 years.",
      "Note 2: for each patient, the total number of 30-day UHRs was summed over the follow-up period, and summary statistics were calculated from these patient-level totals across patients.",
      "Note 3: summary statistics were calculated from patients with at least one index admission (N = 48)."
    )
  )  %>%
  flextable::font(part = "all", fontname = "Century Gothic") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "all", size = 11) %>%
  flextable::italic(part = "footer", italic = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::align(part = "footer", align = "left") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "footer", size = 9)
```

### Maximum number of 30-day UHRs

```{r}
#| label: tbl-descriptive-30-dayUHR-distribution
#| tbl-cap: "Maximum of 30-day UHRs per patient experienced during follow-up"
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'

readmission_distribution <- uhr_by_patient %>%
  group_by(patient_readmissions) %>%
  summarise(count = n()) %>%
  mutate(
    proportion = count / sum(count) * 100,
    Value = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", count, proportion)
  )

readmission_distribution %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    "Maximum number of 30-day UHRs" = patient_readmissions,
    "N patients (%)¹" = Value
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(`Maximum number of 30-day UHRs`, `N patients (%)¹`) %>%
  flextable::regulartable() %>%
  flextable::autofit() %>%
  flextable::bold(part = "header", bold = TRUE) %>% 
  flextable::add_footer_lines(
    values = c(
      "¹ Percentage relative to patients with at least one index admission (N = 48).",
      "Note: Average follow-up time: 5.4 years."
    )
  ) %>%
  flextable::font(part = "all", fontname = "Century Gothic") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "all", size = 11) %>%
  flextable::italic(part = "footer", italic = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "footer", size = 9) %>%  
  flextable::align(j = 1, align = "left", part = "all") %>%  
  flextable::align(j = 2, align = "right", part = "all")
```

## Number of 30-day UHRs events across patient’s age

```{r}
#| label: fig-30-day-readmissions-year-df
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

# prepare data for plotting readmissions by year of age
readmissions_by_years <- readmissions_df %>%
  # flag the year in which the admission has occurred based on admission start
  mutate(age_years = floor(admission_age_days_firstDate / 365.25)) %>%
  # group by patient and year to get the count per patient per year
  group_by(patient_uuid, age_years) %>%
  summarise(
    readmissions = sum(count_readmissions),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # group by year to get the summary across patients per year
  group_by(age_years) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_readmissions = mean(readmissions, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_readmissions = median(readmissions, na.rm = TRUE),
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    age_years = cut(
      age_years,
      breaks = c(0:21, Inf),
      right = FALSE,
      include.lowest = TRUE
    )
  )

# Extract the unique patient_uuid under follow up by age group
# Note: this was obtained from reviewed code from IND submission with subgrouping analysis.
follow_up_patients_uuid <- hospitalization_main_df_nb %>%
  # remove invalid index admissions (2 records)
  filter(!(readmission == "index" & is.na(count_readmissions))) %>%
  group_by(patient_uuid) %>%
  reframe(
    age_range = seq(
      floor(min(first_record_age_days, na.rm = TRUE) / 365.25),
      floor(max(last_record_age_days, na.rm = TRUE) / 365.25)
    )
  ) %>%
  # remove ages > 20 years to compare with graph of 30-day outcome
  filter(age_range <= 20) %>% 
  mutate(
    age_years = cut(
      age_range,
      breaks = c(0:21, Inf),
      right = FALSE,
      include.lowest = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-age_range) %>%
  group_by(age_years) %>%
  reframe(n = n_distinct(patient_uuid))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-30-day-readmissions-year-mean
#| fig-cap: "Mean number of 30-day UHRs per patient by year^[Number of 30-day UHRs were summed per patient within each age interval, and means were computed across patients for each interval.]"
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

fig_readmissions_by_years_mean <-  ggplot() + 
  
  geom_col( 
    data = follow_up_patients_uuid,
    aes(x = age_years, 
      y = n * (1.5/50), 
      fill = "Number of patients with at least one index admission during follow-up"),  
    colour = "grey40",  
    linetype = "dotted",
    width = 0.9, 
    alpha = 0.4           
    ) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Number of patients with at least one index admission during follow-up" = "grey80"), name = NULL) +
  
  # Patient counts as text labels
  geom_text(
  data = follow_up_patients_uuid,
  aes(x = age_years,
      y = n * (1.5/50) + 0.05,   # move text up a bit relative to shorter bars
      label = paste0("n = ", n)),
  size = 2.5, vjust = 0
  )+
  
  # Mean readmissions 
  geom_line(
    data = readmissions_by_years,
    aes(x = age_years, y = mean_readmissions, group = 1),
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = readmissions_by_years,
    aes(x = age_years, y = mean_readmissions),
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Mean number of 30-day UHRs per patient",
    limits = c(0, 3), breaks = seq(0, 3, 1)
  ) +
  labs(x = "Patient's age at admission (years)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold", angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.title   = element_text(hjust = 0),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

fig_readmissions_by_years_mean
```

## Distribution of 30-day UHRs events across patient’s age

```{r}
#| label: fig-30-day-distribution-patient-age-uhrs
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of 30-day UHRs events across patient’s age (years)^[Follow-up duration is defined by patient's first and last medical records from all available records across all datasets as of the most recent data update. Patients without any hospital admissions or valid index admission during their follow-up period are not included in this plot.]"
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| out-width: 100%

# 1) Prepare UHR events on the AGE scale (years)
admission_events_age <- hospitalization_main_df_nb %>%
  # remove invalid index admissions (2 records)
  filter(!(readmission == "index" & is.na(count_readmissions))) %>%
  # keep only index and 30-day UHR events
  filter(grepl("^index$|^30_days_uhr_", readmission)) %>%
  mutate(
    # event occurrence age (years) for plotting as points
    admission_age_years = admission_age_days_firstDate / 365.25,
    readmission_type = dplyr::case_when(
      readmission == "index" ~ "Index admission",
      grepl("^30_days_uhr_", readmission) ~ "30-day UHR"
    )
  )

# 2) Patient observation span on AGE scale (+ numeric y for tiny vertical tick)
patient_followup_age <- hospitalization_main_df_nb %>%
  filter(readmission == "index" & !is.na(count_readmissions)) %>%
  distinct(patient_uuid, first_record_age_days, last_record_age_days) %>%
  mutate(
    first_record_age_years = first_record_age_days / 365.25,
    last_record_age_years  = last_record_age_days  / 365.25,
    followup_duration      = last_record_age_years - first_record_age_years
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(followup_duration)) %>%
  mutate(
    patient_label = factor(row_number(), levels = rev(row_number())),
    patient_y     = as.numeric(patient_label)  # for vertical first record tick
  )

# 3) Merge events with ranked patients
admission_plot_data_age <- admission_events_age %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    patient_followup_age %>% dplyr::select(patient_uuid, patient_label),
    by = "patient_uuid"
  )

# 4. plot the data
fig_distribution_uhrs_age <- ggplot() +
  # Observation span over AGE (dashed)
  geom_linerange(
    data = patient_followup_age,
    aes(
      y = patient_label,
      xmin = first_record_age_years,
      xmax = last_record_age_years
    ),
    linetype = "dashed", color = "black", size = 0.4
  ) +
  # Tiny vertical tick at FIRST medical record
  geom_linerange(
    data = patient_followup_age,
    aes(
      x = first_record_age_years,
      ymin = patient_y - 0.3,
      ymax = patient_y + 0.3,
      color = "Start of follow-up"
    ),
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  # End of observation (diamond at LAST medical record)
  geom_point(
    data = patient_followup_age,
    aes(x = last_record_age_years, y = patient_label, color = "End of follow-up"),
    shape = 18, size = 1.7
  ) +
  # Index admission (orange point)
  geom_point(
    data = admission_plot_data_age %>% dplyr::filter(readmission_type == "Index admission"),
    aes(x = admission_age_years, y = patient_label, color = "Index admission"),
    size = 1.7
  ) +
  # 30-day UHR admissions (blue points)
  geom_point(
    data = admission_plot_data_age %>% dplyr::filter(readmission_type == "30-day UHR"),
    aes(x = admission_age_years, y = patient_label, color = "30-day UHR"),
    size = 1.7
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Event",
    values = c(
      "Index admission"     = "darkorange",
      "30-day UHR"          = "blue",
      "Start of follow-up"= "black",
      "End of follow-up" = "black"
    ),
    breaks = c(
      "Index admission",
      "30-day UHR",
      "Start of follow-up",
      "End of follow-up"
    ) # <-- sets legend order
  ) +
  scale_x_sqrt(breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 8, 12, 18, 24), limits = c(0, 24)) +
  labs(

  ) +

    axis.text.x   = element_text(size = 9,  face = "bold"),
```

## Negative Binomial Mixed Effects model

A **negative binomial (NB) mixed-effects** regression model with random intercept and slope was fitted as the main model to assess the effect of covariates on the rate of 30-day UHR per index admission.

Pre-modelling assumptions for negative binomial models are described in [appendix](#appendix). At first instance the random intercept and slope were included to account for individual variability in baseline readmission number and their change over time. In case of convergence issues, it was recommended to first remove the random slope to ensure model convergence and stability.

The analysis began with a minimal model including only the main timescale (`age_index_admission_yr`). This minimal model was used to check model assumptions (see [Appendix](#appendix)), as well as to ensure stable convergence before introducing additional covariates.

### NB minimal — Linear age (RI + RS) and (RI only)

Linear effect of age with patient-level random intercept and random slope for age.

```{r}
#| label: nb-main-model
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'

#' Mixed effect Negative Binomial model with offset term 
#' with random slope and intercept
#' Note 1: It is fitted a generalized mixed effect model using
#' the negative binomial distribution with a log link, appropriate for 
#' overdispersed count data (Morgans et al 2024). nbinom2 has  a variance that
#'  increases quadratically with the mean (classic NB used in most software)
#' Note 2: source https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/glmmTMB/glmmTMB.pdf
#' Note 3: the offset can be specified in the formula (done below) or 
#' as using argument offset = log(exptime). The first way was preferred as
#' simplify posterior analyses with emmeans.
#' Note 4: linearity of the link function is assumed, meaning that the 
#' relationship between the predictors and the log of the expected count
#' is linear.

nb_model_min <- glmmTMB(
  count_readmissions ~
    age_index_admission_yr +
    offset(log(exptime)) + 
    (1 + age_index_admission_yr | patient_uuid),
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = nb_model_main_df
)

summary(nb_model_min)
```

Linear effect of age with patient-level random intercept only.

```{r}
#| label: nb-main-model-ri-only
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'

nb_model_min_ri_only <- glmmTMB(
  count_readmissions ~
    age_index_admission_yr +
    offset(log(exptime)) + 
    (1 | patient_uuid),
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = nb_model_main_df
)

summary(nb_model_min_ri_only)
```

### NB minimal — Non-linear structural form of time (RCS)

After fitting the minimal model with linear assumption of age, a non-linear structural form of time was explored by applying a **restricted cubic spline (RCS)** transformation of the timescale was applied to the minimal model.

For this model, it was first determined the optimal number of knots for the RCS transformation of age by testing models with 3, 4, and 5 knots and comparing their Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) values. The model with the lowest AIC was selected as the optimal model. In case of convergence issues, the number of knots was reduced until convergence was achieved.

```{r}
#| label: nb-rcs-minimal-test-optimal-knots
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# The function is defined in the functions.R script
#' Note: it was added to the function the argument "control" to help the model
#'  to converge with different knots by following:
#' https://stackoverflow.com/questions/73135114/convergence-criteria-in-glmmtmb-what-are-my-options
optimal_knots <- suppressMessages(
  test_knots_ns_glmmTMB(
    data = nb_model_main_df,
    predictor = "age_index_admission_yr",
    response = "count_readmissions",
    fixed_effects = NULL,
    random_effect = "1 | patient_uuid",
    offset_var = "exptime",
    k_vec = c(3,4,5),
    family = nbinom2(link = "log")
  )
)

optimal_knots
```

The model with 4 knots had the lowest AIC, indicating the best fit among the tested models. Results were consistent when including all covariates (see [appendix](#appendix)). A k = 4 offers an adequate fit of the model and is a good compromise between flexibility and loss of precision caused by overfitting a small sample [@harrellRegressionModelingStrategies2015].

```{r}
#| label: number-knots
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'
#| message: false
#| warning: false

#' Defining knots for the RCS transformation of age
#' Position of knots are based on default quantiles:
#' position at default quantiles with 4 knots:
#' .05 .35 .65 .95 (rcspline.eval vignettes and Harrel 2015) 
knots_rcs <- attributes(rms::rcs(nb_model_main_df$age_index_admission_yr, 4))$parms

# display knots location for age at index admission
paste0("Knots for age at index admission (years): ",
       paste(round(knots_rcs, 2), collapse = ", "))
```

```{r}
#| label: nb-rcs-minimal
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'

# Several tutorials for implementing the rcs in glmTMB package were consulted:
#' https://backend.orbit.dtu.dk/ws/portalfiles/portal/154739064/Publishers_version.pdf
#' https://bora.uib.no/bora-xmlui/bitstream/handle/11250/3145134/51107913.pdf 
#' Note 1: the random slope for time is removed here to ensure model convergence,
#' as the model became too complex: 
#' https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-sig-mixed-models/2018q2/026829.html
#' Note 2: rms::rcs(age_index_admission_yr, parms = knots_rcs) function gives
#'  the same results  when ns() explicity mention the location of the internal
#'   and boundaries knots. 
#' Note 3: Due to the ns() has more examples in the glmmTMB package, it was 
#' preferred to use. Moreover, the ns() has shown less convergence issues when 
#' testing models below.

# Fit the model with RCS transformation of age
nb_model_rcs_min <- glmmTMB(
  count_readmissions ~
    ns(age_index_admission_yr,
       knots = knots_rcs[2:3], # internal knots
       Boundary.knots = c(knots_rcs[1], knots_rcs[4])) + # boundary knots
    offset(log(exptime)) +
    (1 | patient_uuid),
  data = nb_model_main_df,
  family = nbinom2(link = "log")
  )

# Model summary
summary(nb_model_rcs_min)
```

### Comparing performance of minimal models

```{r}
#| label: tbl-nb-performance-comparison-minimal
#| tbl-cap: "Comparing performance of minimal models based on different performance indices"
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'

compare_performance(nb_model_min, # mixed effect NB minimal model
                    nb_model_min_ri_only, # with random intercept only
                    nb_model_rcs_min) # with restricted cubic splines
```

The negative binomial mixed-effects model with RCS transformation of age provided a better fit between proposed minimal models (@tbl-nb-performance-comparison-minimal) and it has also satisfied the assumptions of the model (see [appendix](#appendix)).Therefore, this model was used as the basis for further analyses.

### Covariate selection

Given the small sample size, starting with the full model risked overfitting, inflated standard errors, and instability in the selection process. Therefore, to ensure a statistically and computationally stable model, covariate selection was performed using the Buildmer package, which is suited for models fitted with the glmmTMB framework as first identifies the **maximal feasible model** and then applies a **stepwise backward elimination** procedure based on the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) [@voetenBuildmerStepwiseElimination2025].

Specifically, the process begins with the forced terms (non-linear age at index admission, patient sex, and random effects) and sequentially adds other covariates according to their contribution to model fit, as measured by the AIC. Once the maximal feasible model is reached, Buildmer automatically applies backward elimination to remove covariates that do not improve model fit, yielding the final optimal model.

Additionally, to assess the robustness of the covariates retained through these selection procedures, a model averaging approach was applied (see [appendix](#appendix)):

a.  All possible combinations of covariates were evaluated from the maximal/full model with the dredge function from MuMIn package. The model with the lowest AIC was identified, and all models with ΔAIC \< 2 were extracted for the next step.

b.  The sum of Akaike weights for each covariate was calculated, highlighting those that consistently contributed to model fit across competing model specifications [@maesUsingMultimodelInference2021; @fletcherWhyModelAveraging2018].

*Note: the stepwise selection was also manually tested, yielding the same results to the automatic procedure (results not shown)*

##### Automatic backward stepwise feature selection

```{r}
#| label: nb-main-model-stepwise-automatic
#| echo: false
#| eval: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# Note: Tutorials were consulted for the automatic stepwise selection:
#' https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/buildmer/buildmer.pdf
#' https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/664985/retaining-fixed-effects-during-buildglmmtmb

#' formula: all covariates without forced, random effects and offset as are 
#' specified in the buildmerControl include argument
f <- count_readmissions ~ neonatal_onset + other_epilepsy_mutations +
  recurrent_variant + seizure_related_index_admission +
  length_of_index_stay_days_cat + respiratory_support_index_admission +
  tech_assistance_ever + vns_insertion_ever + n_distinct_asm_index_admission +
  adverse_effect_index_admission +
  ketogenic_diet_admission + quinidine_admission

stepwise_backward_test <- buildmer::buildglmmTMB(
  #' keep the same full list stated when maximal feasible model was built as 
  #' the order step will be applied again
  f, 
  data = nb_model_main_df,
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  buildmerControl = buildmerControl(
    #' force terms (sex, age, random effects and offset) not subject 
    #' to testing for elimination. 
    include = ~ ns(age_index_admission_yr,
       knots = knots_rcs[2:3],
       Boundary.knots = c(knots_rcs[1], knots_rcs[4])) +
      sex + offset(log(exptime)) + (1 | patient_uuid),
    #' 1. The order step is useful if the maximal model includes random effects: 
    #' buildmer will start out with an empty model and keeps adding terms to
    #'  this model until convergence can no longer be achieved.
    #' 2.  ordered backward elimination means that first reach the maximal 
    #' feasible model and then eliminate terms one by one.
    direction = c('order', 'backward'), 
    #' Criterion used to test terms for their contribution to the model fit
    crit = 'AIC',
    #' Criterion used to test terms for elimination in the elimination step
    elim = 'AIC'
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: nb-main-model-stepwise-automatic-output-formula
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| results: 'markup'
#| message: false

# note: the output was saved in r rds file as takes few minutes to run.
# dir.create("~/RWE-rare_disease/Hospitalizations/output/rds_data")
# saveRDS(stepwise_backward_test, "rds_data/automatic_stepwise_backward_test.rds")

# Load the saved stepwise backward file
stepwise_backward_test_file <- readRDS("rds_data/automatic_stepwise_backward_test.rds")

# assign the formula from the stepwise backward
automatic_backward_stepwise <- formula(stepwise_backward_test_file@model)

# print the formula
automatic_backward_stepwise
```

The automatic backward stepwise selection procedure removed four covariates from the maximal feasible model: `vns_insertion_ever`, `tech_assistance_ever`, `neonatal_onset`, `respiratory_support_index_admission`.

```{r}
#| label: nb-rcs-stepwise-automatic-selection
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'

# Fit the automatic stepwise model for further comparisons
nb_model_rcs_stepwise <- glmmTMB(
  # formula from the automatic stepwise selection
  formula = automatic_backward_stepwise,
  data = nb_model_main_df,
  family = nbinom2(link = "log")
)

summary(nb_model_rcs_stepwise)
```

The robustness of the stepwise selection results was further evaluated through model averaging across all possible covariate combinations (see [appendix](#appendix)).This assessment confirmed the stepwise model (`nb_model_rcs_stepwise`) as the an appropriate **main effects model** for subsequent analyses.

The final reteained covariates were: `sex`, `age_index_admission_yr`, `other_epilepsy_mutations`, `recurrent_variant`. `adverse_effect_index_admission`, `length_of_index_stay_days_cat`, `quinidine_admission`, `ketogenic_diet_admission`, `seizure_related_index_admission` and `n_distinct_asm_index_admission`.

### Testing inteaction terms

An interaction between two variables implies that the effect of each variable is not constant over levels of the other variable [@harrellRegressionModelingStrategies2013]. In the present analysis, interactions were considered not only because of their potential clinical relevance in identifying subgroups with different risk profiles, but also to improve model fit by allowing the additional flexibility provided by interaction terms [@vanderweeleTutorialInteraction2014].

Given the limited prior evidence on potential interactions between covariates for rare_disease, it was focused on testing interactions of retained covariates with age at admission. Interaction terms were added one by one to the main effects model obtained in the previous step, and the goodness of fit was assessed using AIC and the Likelihood Ratio Test (LRT) to compare the model without interaction terms [@harrellRegressionModelingStrategies2013].

Interaction term which significantly improved the model fit were retained in the final model after checking comparison graphs and clinical plausibility.

#### Age at index admission with sex

```{r}
        knots_rcs[4]))*sex +

    adverse_effect_index_admission + 
    recurrent_variant + 
    other_epilepsy_mutations +

    ketogenic_diet_admission +

  data = nb_model_main_df
)

# the interaction does not significantly improves the goodness of fit of the model.
anova(nb_model_rcs_stepwise, nb_model_rcs_int_sex_age)
```


A total of two interactions were found to significantly improve the model fit when added one by one to the main effects model, as assessed by LRT (p \< 0.05). These were:

-   `age × seizure-related index admission`

-   `age × number of ASMs at index admission`

Considering clinical relevance and model parsimony, the interaction `age × seizure-related index admission` was selected to be included in the final model. Seizure-related hospitalizations are more common in younger patients with epilepsy, and the risk of readmission may vary with age in this group.

Although the `age_admission_yr` x `number of ASMs at index admission` was statistically significant by LRT, the observed differences occurred mainly at older ages where very few patients were available for comparison. This resulted in unstable estimates with wide confidence intervals, limiting the reliability of the effect.

For this reason, that interaction was finally not included in the **preliminary final model**:

```{r}
#| label: nb-model-stepwise-interactions
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'
#| warning: false

nb_model_rcs_stepwise_interactions <- glmmTMB(
  count_readmissions ~
    offset(log(exptime)) + 
    ns(age_index_admission_yr, 
       knots = knots_rcs[2:3], 
       Boundary.knots = c(knots_rcs[1],
                          knots_rcs[4]))*seizure_related_index_admission +
    sex +
    adverse_effect_index_admission +
    length_of_index_stay_days_cat +
    recurrent_variant +
    other_epilepsy_mutations +
    quinidine_admission +
    ketogenic_diet_admission +
    n_distinct_asm_index_admission +
    (1 | patient_uuid),
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = nb_model_main_df,
  # add control options to help the model converge
  control = glmmTMBControl(
    optimizer = optim,
    optArgs = list(method = "BFGS")
  )
)

summary(nb_model_rcs_stepwise_interactions)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

compare_performance(
```

The model with the interaction terms `age × seizure-related index admission` had a better fit for the AIC than the main effects model (@tbl-nb-performance-stepwise-interaction).

The `nb_model_rcs_stepwise_interactions` was defined as the **final model** for conducting the next steps of statistical outputs for main analyses.

The final model has converged properly and satisfied the model assumptions (see [appendix](#appendix)).

:::

```{r}

table_regression_nb <- tbl_regression(
  nb_model_rcs_stepwise_interactions,
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  conf.level = 0.95,
  label = list(
    sex = "Sex",
    other_epilepsy_mutations = "Other epilepsy mutations",
    recurrent_variant = "Highly recurrent variant",
    length_of_index_stay_days_cat = "Length of index hospital stay",

    quinidine_admission = "Quinidine treatment during index admission",

  # remove issue with group(cond) column
  tidy_fun = function(x, ...) {

      dplyr::select(-component)   
  }) %>%
  modify_header(estimate = "**IRR**") %>%
  modify_table_body(~ dplyr::select(., -p.value)) %>%
  bold_labels() %>%
  italicize_levels()


# Rename levels for binary variables
table_regression_nb$table_body <- table_regression_nb$table_body %>%
  mutate(label = case_when(
    label == "0" ~ "No",
    label == "1" ~ "Yes",
    label == "male" ~ "Male",
    label == "female" ~ "Female",
    TRUE ~ label
  ))

# Remove the spline rows explicitly and the interaction term row
table_regression_nb$table_body <- table_regression_nb$table_body %>%
  filter(!str_detect(variable, "^ns\\(age_index_admission_yr")) %>%
  filter(!str_detect(variable, "^seizure_related_index_admission")) %>%
  filter(!str_detect(variable, "patient_uuid"))

# print the table with kableExtra
tbl_regression_nb <- table_regression_nb %>%
  modify_footnote(
    estimate ~ paste(
      "IRR = Incidence Rate Ratio. IRR > 1 indicates a higher rate of 30-day UHRs; IRR < 1 indicates a lower rate.",
      "For categorical predictors, IRRs compare each level with the reference category.",
      "For continuous predictors, IRRs correspond to the rate change per 1-unit increase in the predictor.",
      "Estimates are adjusted for all variables in the model. Nonlinear spline terms and random-effect estimates are not reported.",
      sep = " "
    )
  ) %>%
  as_flex_table() %>%
  flextable::font(fontname = "Century Gothic", part = "all") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(size = 11, part = "all") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "footer", size = 9) %>%  
  flextable::autofit()

tbl_regression_nb
```

### Marginal means estimations

For clarity, we present two separate EMM summaries from the same fitted model: (1) overall age effects obtained by averaging over covariates and retained interaction terms; and (2) stratified age effects estimated conditional on seizure-related status to illustrate the interaction. The second set was not computed from the first and both come directly from the final fitted model (`nb_model_rcs_stepwise_interactions`).

#### Main effect of age at index admission

##### Table: predicted 30-day UHR across age at index admission

```{r}
#| label: tbl-emmeans-table
#| tbl-cap: "Overall estimated marginal means of 30-day UHR number per 100 index admissions."
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'
#| warning: false

# Estimate marginal means (with 95% CI) of readmission rates by age at admission
# - adjusted to mean observed exposure time (29.888 days)
# - averaging over all other covariates (nuisance factors) with equal weights
# - results reported on natural scale (rate or count) at specified ages (0–20 years)
#' https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/emmeans/vignettes/messy-data.html#nuisance
#' https://rvlenth.github.io/emmeans/articles/sophisticated.html?q=offset#offsets
#' https://rvlenth.github.io/emmeans/articles/xplanations.html#offsets
#' https://m-clark.github.io/posts/2020-06-15-predict-with-offset/

# Define the sequence of ages (in years) at which to estimate marginal means
# From 0 to 5 by 0.5
age_first_seq <- seq(0, 5, by = 0.5)

# From 6 to 18 by 1
age_second_seq <- seq(6, 18, by = 1)

# Combine the two sequences
age_seq <- c(age_first_seq, age_second_seq)

# Build the reference grid explicitly
#' non.nuisance = "age_index_admission_yr" ensures age is not averaged 
#' (we want to see estimates for specific time points)
#' all other predictors (nuisance factors) are averaged over equally
grid_emmeans_full <- ref_grid(
  nb_model_rcs_stepwise_interactions, # final model with interactions
  at = list(age_index_admission_yr = age_seq),
  non.nuisance = "age_index_admission_yr", # do not average
  params = "knots_rcs",  # state knot values for the splines model,
  weights = "equal" # average others with equal weights
)

# https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/499089/emmeans-output-interpretation-of-a-glmer-fit-with-nesting
# https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79489617/how-to-extract-std-dev-from-varcorr-glmmtmb
#' Define total standard deviation for bias adjustment (only random is given
#'  in glmmtmb models)
cor_random_mod <- lme4::VarCorr(nb_model_rcs_stepwise_interactions)
total_sd <- sapply(cor_random_mod$cond, function(x) attr(x, "stddev"))

#' Model with offset, weights assumed equal
readmissions_by_age <- emmeans(
  grid_emmeans_full, ~ age_index_admission_yr,
  type = "response", # results back-transformed to the natural scale 
  #' use of offset in emmeans to get the rate per adjusted index 
  offset = mean(log(nb_model_main_df$exptime)), # same as default and ≈ log(30)
  # Note: Note that the random effects variance is close to zero, so bias 
  # adjustment has literally no effect here.
  bias.adj = TRUE, # bias adjustment for back-transforming from log scale
  sigma = total_sd # include the standard deviation of the random effect
  )

# Convert the emmeans object to a regular dataframe
readmissions_by_age_df <- as.data.frame(readmissions_by_age)

# View results
# Scaling up the number per 100 index with respective IC95% for interpretation
#'https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/reports/statbriefs/sb304-readmissions-2016-2020.jsp 
#' https://www.bmj.com/content/366/bmj.l4563.abstract

#' Note: emmeans on glmmTMB models uses asymptotic Wald (z) inference, so
#' degrees of freedom are treated as Inf and CIs appear as asymp.LCL/UCL.
tbl_readmissions_by_age_df <- readmissions_by_age_df %>%
  mutate(
    combined = sprintf(
      "%.1f (%.1f; %.1f)",
      response * 100, asymp.LCL * 100, asymp.UCL * 100
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(age_index_admission_yr, combined) %>%
  rename(
    "Age at index admission (years)" = age_index_admission_yr,
    "Number of 30-day UHRs per 100 index admissions (95% CI)" = combined
  ) %>%
  flextable::regulartable() %>%
  flextable::autofit() %>%
  flextable::bold(part = "header", bold = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::add_footer_lines(values = c(
    "Note 1: the endpoint was scaled to 100 index admissions as standard practice to facilitate interpretation.",
    "Note 2: results indicate, at each age, how many 30-day unplanned readmissions would be expected for every 100 index admissions (or 100 discharges)."
  )) %>%
  flextable::font(part = "all", fontname = "Century Gothic") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "all", size = 11) %>%
  flextable::italic(part = "footer", italic = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::align(part = "footer", align = "left") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "footer", size = 9) %>%
  flextable::align(j = 1, part = "all", align = "left") %>%
  flextable::align(j = 2, part = "all", align = "center")

tbl_readmissions_by_age_df
```

##### Contrast between time points of interest

```{r}
#| label: tbl-contrast-time-points-model-nb
#| tbl-cap: "Pairwise contrast for time-points of interest (6, 12, 18, and 24 months)"
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| results: 'markup'

# obtain time point of interest to compare from the total emmeans grid
# Pairwise comparisons at 6, 12, 18, and 24 months of life using t-tests and 
# the Kenward-Roger's approximation of the degrees of freedom.
emm_subset_nb_main <- subset(readmissions_by_age, 
                             age_index_admission_yr %in% c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2))
 
# time point comparison
# Using wald tests based on the asymptotic distribution of the estimates
contrast_nb_main <- emmeans::contrast(emm_subset_nb_main,
                                      method = "pairwise", # all pairwise comparisons
                                      ref = 1, # reference is 0.5 years
                                      adjust = "tukey"
                                      )

tbl_contrast_nb_main <- contrast_nb_main %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::select(-c("df", "null", "z.ratio")) %>%
  transmute(
    `Contrasted time-points (years)` =
      str_squish(str_replace_all(contrast, c("age_index_admission_yr" = "", "/" = " vs "))),
    Ratio = ratio,
    SE = SE,
    `P value` = case_when(
      p.value < 1e-4 ~ "< 0.0001",
      p.value < 0.05 ~ "< 0.05",
      TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", p.value)
    )
  ) %>%
  flextable::regulartable() %>%
  flextable::autofit() %>%
  flextable::colformat_double(j = c("Ratio", "SE"), digits = 2) %>%
  flextable::bold(part = "header", bold = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::add_footer_lines(
    values = c(
      "Note 1: Tukey-adjusted wald tests performed on the log scale, based on the asymptotic distribution of the estimates.",
      "Note 2: P-values < 0.05 indicate that the predicted number of 30-day UHRs at the contrasted time points were significantly different."
    )
  ) %>%
  flextable::font(part = "all", fontname = "Century Gothic") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "all", size = 11) %>%
  flextable::italic(part = "footer", italic = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::align(part = "footer", align = "left") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "footer", size = 9) 

tbl_contrast_nb_main
```

#### Interaction effect of age at index admission and seizure-related index admission

##### Table: predicted 30-day UHR across age at index admission

```{r}
#| label: tbl-emmeans-table-interactions
#| tbl-cap: "Estimated marginal means of the number of 30-day UHR per 100 index admissions by selected time points for seizure-related and non-seizure related index admissions."
#| echo: false

grid_by_seizure <- ref_grid(
  nb_model_rcs_stepwise_interactions,
  at = list(age_index_admission_yr = age_seq),
  # do not average the interaction terms to get the values per time point
  non.nuisance = c("age_index_admission_yr", "seizure_related_index_admission"), 
  params = "knots_rcs",
  weights = "equal" # average others with equal weights
)

readmissions_by_age_int <- emmeans(
  # add the interaction term to the grid
  grid_by_seizure, ~ age_index_admission_yr | seizure_related_index_admission,
  type = "response", 
  offset = mean(log(nb_model_main_df$exptime)),
  bias.adj = TRUE, # bias adjustment for log link back-transformation
  sigma = total_sd # include the standard deviation of the random effect
  )

# Convert the emmeans object to a regular dataframe
readmissions_by_age_int_df <- as.data.frame(readmissions_by_age_int)

  mutate(
    grp = ifelse(seizure_related_index_admission == 1, "SR", "NSR"),

  dplyr::select(age = age_index_admission_yr, grp, val) %>%

  flextable::set_header_labels(

    colwidths = c(1, 2)

  values = c(
```

# Sensitivity analysis

Merging admission records into continuous hospitalization episode may help mitigate the overestimation of hospital admission events due to potential transfers to a different hospital or within the same hospital in rwd_source’s patients.

To assess this, the main analysis was repeated under two different scenarios in which raw hospital admissions records occurring on the same day or the day after last discharge will be merged into a single hospitalization episode. For each scenario, the merged hospital admission:

-   Used the earliest admission date as the start date,

-   Used the latest discharge date as the end date and,

-   Was performed only when the admissions had the same type of diagnosis (i.e., both admissions with a seizure-related type or both admissions with a non-seizure-related type). If types differed between admission, the records remained separated.

The main analysis was repeated for each scenario.

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}

## Sensitivity analysis (I): Merging hospital admission records occurring on the same day after last discharge

```{r}
#| label: sensitivity-analyses-merging-admissions-same-day-rename
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

# Select, order and rename variables for readmission df
#' Note1: readmission variable used to filter the desired subset of data
#' was derived in the data management file, in the sensitivity analysis section
#' Note2: Index derived in the data management file already excludes planned, birth
# and outpatient admissions
readmissions_merged_same_day_df <- hospitalizations_merged_same_day_df %>%
  #' keep index with valid exptime and remove those with invalid index 
  #' admission which doens't allow to count readmissions (i.e. exptime == 0)
  filter(readmission == "index" & !is.na(count_readmissions)) %>%
  # order, rename and select variables of interest
  dplyr::select(
    # patient identifier
    patient_uuid,
    # admissions related features
    admission_age_days_firstDate,
    admission_age_days_lastDate,
    # demographics
    sex,
    age_index_admission_yr = age_admission_yr,
    # genetic mutations
    other_epilepsy_mutations,
    recurrent_variant,
    neonatal_onset,
    # clinical history
    seizure_related_index_admission = seizure_related_admission,
    length_of_index_stay_days_cat = length_of_stay_days_cat,
    respiratory_support_index_admission = respiratory_support_admission,
    tech_assistance_ever,
    count_readmissions,
    exptime,
    # treatment history
    vns_insertion_ever,
    n_distinct_asm_index_admission = n_distinct_asm_admission,
    adverse_effect_index_admission = adverse_effect_admission,
    ketogenic_diet_admission,
    quinidine_admission
    )
```

### NB minimal - Linear age (RI + RS)

Pre and post modelling assumptions were checked (see [appendix](#appendix)).

```{r}
#| label: model-same-day-nb-minimal
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'

nb_model_min_sensit_same_day <- glmmTMB(
  count_readmissions ~
    age_index_admission_yr +
    offset(log(exptime)) + 
    (1 + age_index_admission_yr | patient_uuid),
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = nb_model_sensit_df_same_day
)

summary(nb_model_min_sensit_same_day)
```

### NB minimal model - Non-lineal structural form of time (RCS)

```{r}
#| label: nb-rcs-minimal-test-optimal-knots-sensit-same-day
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'
#| message: false
#| warning: false

#'the function has the control argument to help the model converge when
#'testing the optimal number.
optimal_knots_same_day <- suppressMessages(
  test_knots_ns_glmmTMB(
    data = nb_model_sensit_df_same_day,
    predictor = "age_index_admission_yr",
    response = "count_readmissions",
    fixed_effects = NULL,
    random_effect = "1 | patient_uuid",
    offset_var = "exptime",
    k_vec = c(3,4,5),
    family = nbinom2(link = "log")
  )
)

optimal_knots_same_day
```

The optimal number of knots was tested with the minimal model was 4 knots.

```{r}
#| label: number_knots-sensit-same-day
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'
#| message: false
#| warning: false

#' Defining knots for RCS
#' default positions at quantiles 5th, 35th, 65th, and 95th
knots_rcs_same_day <- attributes(rms::rcs(
  nb_model_sensit_df_same_day$age_index_admission_yr, 4))$parms

# display knots location for age at index admission
paste0("Knots for age at index admission (years): ",
       paste(round(knots_rcs_same_day, 2), collapse = ", "))
```

```{r}
#| label: model-same-day-nb-rcs-minimal
#| echo: false

# fit the stepwise model with merged admissions for same day of discharge
nb_model_rcs_min_sensit_same_day <- glmmTMB(
  count_readmissions ~ 
    ns(age_index_admission_yr, 
       knots = knots_rcs_same_day[2:3], # internal knots
       Boundary.knots = c(knots_rcs_same_day[1], knots_rcs_same_day[4])) + # boundary knots
    offset(log(exptime)) + 
    (1 | patient_uuid),
  data = nb_model_sensit_df_same_day,
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  # add control to help convergence issues
  control = glmmTMBControl(
    optimizer = optim,
    optArgs = list(method = "BFGS")
  ))

summary(nb_model_rcs_min_sensit_same_day)
```

### Comparing performance of minimal models

```{r}
#| label: tbl-nb-performance-comparison-minimal-sensit-same-day
#| tbl-cap: "Comparing performance of minimal models based on differernt performance indices"
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'

compare_performance(nb_model_min_sensit_same_day, # full model
                    nb_model_min_sensit_only_ri_same_day, # only random intercept
                    nb_model_rcs_min_sensit_same_day) # with restricted cubic splines
```

The model with RCS improved the model fit compared to the minimal model without RCS (@tbl-nb-performance-comparison-minimal-sensit-same-day) and it has satisfied the modelling assumptions (see [appendix](#appendix)). Therefore, the model with RCS was used for further analysis.

### Covariate selection

The same process as described in the main analyses was repeated for this sensitivity analysis.

##### Automatic stepwise selection

```{r}
#| label: nb-main-model-stepwise-automatic-sensit-same-day
#| echo: false
#| eval: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

stepwise_backward_test_same_day <- buildmer::buildglmmTMB(
  #' keep the same full list stated when maximal feasible model was built as
  #' the order step will be applied again
  f,
  data = nb_model_sensit_df_same_day,
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  buildmerControl = buildmerControl(
    # forced terms
    include = ~ ns(age_index_admission_yr,
      knots = knots_rcs_same_day[2:3],
      Boundary.knots = c(
        knots_rcs_same_day[1], knots_rcs_same_day[4])) +
      sex + offset(log(exptime)) + (1 | patient_uuid),
    #' Note: 'order' had been specified again due to the 'backward' alone
    #' removed the forced terms.
    direction = c("order", "backward"),
    #' Criterion used to test terms for their contribution to the model fit
    crit = "AIC",
    #' Criterion used to test terms for elimination in the elimination step
    elim = "AIC",
    #' it was added due to convergence issues in the minimal model 
    #' when adding var sex.
    args = list(control = glmmTMBControl(
      optimizer = optim,
      optArgs = list(method = "BFGS")
    ))
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: nb-main-model-stepwise-automatic-sensit-same-day-print
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| results: 'markup'
#| message: false
# note: the output was saved in r rds file as takes time to run
# dir.create("~/RWE-rare_disease/Hospitalizations/output/rds_data")
#saveRDS(stepwise_backward_test_same_day, "rds_data/automatic_stepwise_backward_test_same_day.rds")

# Load the saved stepwise backward test file
stepwise_backward_test_same_day_file <- readRDS("rds_data/automatic_stepwise_backward_test_same_day.rds")

# assing the formula from the stepwise backward test
automatic_backward_stepwise_same_day <- formula(stepwise_backward_test_same_day_file@model)

# print the formula
automatic_backward_stepwise_same_day
```

The automatic backward stepwise selection procedure removed five covariates from the maximal feasible model: `vns_insertion_ever`, `neonatal_onset`, `tech_assistance_ever`, `n_distinct_asm_index_admission` and `ketogenic_diet_admission`.

```{r}
#| label: nb-rcs-stepwise-automatic-selection-same-day
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'

nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_same_day <- glmmTMB(
  # formula from the automatic stepwise selection
  formula = automatic_backward_stepwise_same_day,
  data = nb_model_sensit_df_same_day,
  family = nbinom2(link = "log")
)

summary(nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_same_day)
```

The robustness of the stepwise selection results was further evaluated through model averaging across all possible covariate combinations (see [appendix](#appendix)).This assessment confirmed the stepwise model (`nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_same_day`) as the an appropriate **main effects model** for subsequent analyses.

The obtained main effects model retained the following covariates: `sex`, `age_index_admission_yr`, `other_epilepsy_mutations`, `recurrent_variant`, `adverse_effect_index_admission`, `length_of_index_stay_days_cat`, `quinidine_admission`, `respiratory_support_index_admission` and `seizure_related_index_admission`.

### Testing inteaction terms

The interaction terms were added one by one to the main effects model obtained in the previous step, and the goodness of fit was assessed using AIC and the LRT to compare the model without interaction terms as performed for the main analyses.

#### Age at index admission with sex

```{r}
#| label: interaction-terms-sex-age-same-day
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'
#| warning: false

nb_model_rcs_int_sex_age_same_day <- glmmTMB(
  count_readmissions ~
    offset(log(exptime)) + 
    ns(age_index_admission_yr,  
    knots = knots_rcs_same_day[2:3], Boundary.knots = c(knots_rcs_same_day[1],  
        knots_rcs_same_day[4]))*sex +
    length_of_index_stay_days_cat + 
    other_epilepsy_mutations +
    adverse_effect_index_admission + 
    recurrent_variant + 
    seizure_related_index_admission +
    quinidine_admission + 
    respiratory_support_index_admission +
    (1 | patient_uuid),
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = nb_model_sensit_df_same_day,
  control = glmmTMBControl(
    optimizer = optim,
    optArgs = list(method = "BFGS")
  )
)

# the interaction does not significantly improves the goodness of fit of the model.
anova(nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_same_day, nb_model_rcs_int_sex_age_same_day)
```

#### Age at index admission with quinidine treatment during index admission


One covariate had an interaction with `age_index_admission_yr` that significantly (p \< 0.05) improved the goodness of fit of the model:

-   `age_index_admission_yr`\*`seizure_related_index_admission`

After discussing with epidemiologists, it was recommended at first instance to include only the interaction between `age_index_admission_yr` and `seizure_related_index_admission` in the model due to the clinical relevance. Further discussions will be held to decide if to include also other interactions.

The **preliminary final model**, which included the interaction terms, was fitted as follows:

```{r}
#| label: nb-model-stepwise-interactions-same-day
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'
#| warning: false

nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_same_day_interactions <- glmmTMB(
  count_readmissions ~
    offset(log(exptime)) +
    ns(age_index_admission_yr,
      knots = knots_rcs_same_day[2:3],
      Boundary.knots = c(
        knots_rcs_same_day[1],
        knots_rcs_same_day[4]))*seizure_related_index_admission +
    sex +
    length_of_index_stay_days_cat +
    other_epilepsy_mutations +
    adverse_effect_index_admission +
    recurrent_variant +
    quinidine_admission +
    respiratory_support_index_admission +
    (1 | patient_uuid),
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = nb_model_sensit_df_same_day,
  control = glmmTMBControl(
    optimizer = optim,
    optArgs = list(method = "BFGS")
  )
)

summary(nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_same_day_interactions)
```

##### Comparing performance

```{r}
#| label: tbl-nb-performance-comparison-interaction-no-interactions-same-day
#| tbl-cap: "Comparing performance of models with and without interaction terms"
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'

compare_performance(nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_same_day, # full model
                    nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_same_day_interactions) # with restricted cubic splines
```

The model with the interaction terms had a lower AIC than the model without interaction terms.

The model with the interaction terms was selected as the **final model** for the sensitivity analyses. It has converged properly and satisfied the model assumptions (see [appendix](#appendix)).

### Statistical ouptus

#### Overall effects of covariates on the rate of 30-day UHR per index admission

```{r}
#| label: tbl-regression_final-same-day
#| tbl-cap: "Adjusted incidence rate ratios (IRRs) for 30-day UHRs for final multivariable model (fixed effects)."
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'

table_regression_nb_same_day <- tbl_regression(
  # final selected model
  nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_same_day_interactions, 
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  conf.level = 0.95,
  label = list(
    sex = "Sex",
    other_epilepsy_mutations = "Other epilepsy mutations",
    recurrent_variant = "Recurrent variant",
    length_of_index_stay_days_cat = "Length of index hospital stay",
    tech_assistance_ever = "History of technology assistance at index admission",
    adverse_effect_index_admission = "Adverse effect during index admission",
    quinidine_admission = "Quinidine treatment during index admission",
    respiratory_support_index_admission = "Respiratory support during index admission"
  ),
    # remove issue with group(cond) column
  tidy_fun = function(x, ...) {
    broom.mixed::tidy(x, component = "cond", ...) %>%
      dplyr::select(-component)   
  }) %>%
  # Rename estimate column to IRR
  modify_header(estimate = "**IRR**") %>%
  # Remove p-values cleanly
  modify_table_body(~ dplyr::select(., -p.value)) %>%
  bold_labels() %>%
  italicize_levels()

# Rename levels for binary variables
table_regression_nb_same_day$table_body <- table_regression_nb_same_day$table_body %>%
  mutate(label = case_when(
    label == "0" ~ "No",
    label == "1" ~ "Yes",
    label == "male" ~ "Male",
    label == "female" ~ "Female",
    TRUE ~ label
  ))

# Remove the spline rows explicitly
table_regression_nb_same_day$table_body <- table_regression_nb_same_day$table_body %>%
  filter(
    !str_detect(variable, "^ns\\(age_index_admission_yr") &
    !str_detect(variable, "seizure_related_index_admission") &
    !str_detect(variable, "patient_uuid")
  )

# Print the table with kableExtra
tbl_regression_nb_same_day <- table_regression_nb_same_day %>%
  modify_footnote(
    estimate ~ paste(
      "IRR = Incidence Rate Ratio. IRR > 1 indicates a higher rate of 30-day UHRs; IRR < 1 indicates a lower rate.",
      "For categorical predictors, IRRs compare each level with the reference category.",
      "For continuous predictors, IRRs correspond to the rate change per 1-unit increase in the predictor.",
      "Estimates are adjusted for all variables in the model. Nonlinear spline terms and random-effect estimates are not reported.",
      sep = " "
    )
  ) %>%
  as_flex_table() %>%
  flextable::font(fontname = "Century Gothic", part = "all") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(size = 11, part = "all") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "footer", size = 9) %>%  
  flextable::autofit()

tbl_regression_nb_same_day
```

#### Marginal means estimations

##### Main effect of age at index admission

###### Table: predicted 30-day UHR across age at index admission

```{r}
#| label: tbl-emmeans-table-sensit-same-day
#| tbl-cap: "Overall estimated marginal means of the number of 30-day UHR per 100 index admissions."
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'
#| warning: false

# Build the reference grid explicitly
grid_emmeans_full_same_day <- ref_grid(
  nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_same_day_interactions,
  at = list(age_index_admission_yr = age_seq), # age seq as defined in main analyses
  non.nuisance = "age_index_admission_yr", # do not average
  params = "knots_rcs_same_day",  # state knot values for the splines model
  weights = "equal" # weights assumed equal
)

# Define total standard deviation for bias adjustment (only random is given)
cor_random_mod_same_day <- lme4::VarCorr(
  nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_same_day_interactions)
total_sd_same_day <- sapply(
  cor_random_mod_same_day$cond, function(x) attr(x, "stddev"))

#' Model with offset, weights assumed equal
readmissions_by_age_same_day <- emmeans(
  grid_emmeans_full_same_day, ~ age_index_admission_yr,
  type = "response",  
  offset = mean(log(nb_model_sensit_df_same_day$exptime)),
  bias.adjust = TRUE, # apply bias adjustment
  sigma = total_sd_same_day # total standard deviation for bias adjustment
  )

# Convert the emmeans object to a regular dataframe
readmissions_by_age_same_day_df <- as.data.frame(readmissions_by_age_same_day)

# View the updated dataframe
tbl_readmissions_by_age_same_day_df <- readmissions_by_age_same_day_df %>%
  mutate(
    combined = sprintf(
      "%.1f (%.1f; %.1f)",
      response * 100, asymp.LCL * 100, asymp.UCL * 100
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(age_index_admission_yr, combined) %>%
  rename(
    "Age at index admission (years)" = age_index_admission_yr,
    "Number of 30-day UHRs per 100 index admissions (95% CI)" = combined
  ) %>%
  flextable::regulartable() %>%
  flextable::autofit() %>%
  flextable::bold(part = "header", bold = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::add_footer_lines(values = c(
    "Note 1: the endpoint was scaled to 100 index admissions as standard practice to facilitate interpretation.",
    "Note 2: results indicate, at each age, how many 30-day unplanned readmissions would be expected for every 100 index admissions (or 100 discharges)."
  )) %>%
  flextable::font(part = "all", fontname = "Century Gothic") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "all", size = 11) %>%
  flextable::italic(part = "footer", italic = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::align(part = "footer", align = "left") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "footer", size = 9) %>%
  flextable::align(j = 1, part = "all", align = "left") %>%
  flextable::align(j = 2, part = "all", align = "center")
```

###### Contrast for time points of interest

```{r}
#| label: tbl-contrast-time-points-same-day
#| tbl-cap: "Pairwise contrast for time-points of interest (6, 12, 18, and 24 months)"
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| results: 'markup'

# obtain time point of interest to compare from the total emmeans grid
emm_subset_nb_full_model_int_same_day <- subset(readmissions_by_age_same_day, 
                                   age_index_admission_yr %in% c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2))

# time point comparison
# pairs(emm_subset) # simplified version of contrast function with same results
contrast_nb_full_model_int_same_day <- emmeans::contrast(
  emm_subset_nb_full_model_int_same_day,
  method = "pairwise",
  ref = 1, # reference is 0.5 years
  adjust = "tukey"
)


tbl_contrast_nb_full_model_int_same_day <- contrast_nb_full_model_int_same_day %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::select(-c("df", "null", "z.ratio")) %>%
  transmute(
    `Contrasted time-points (years)` =
      str_squish(str_replace_all(contrast, c("age_index_admission_yr" = "", "/" = " vs "))),
    Ratio = ratio,
    SE = SE,
    `P value` = case_when(
      p.value < 1e-4 ~ "< 0.0001",
      p.value < 0.05 ~ "< 0.05",
      TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", p.value)
    )
  ) %>%
  flextable::regulartable() %>%
  flextable::autofit() %>%
  flextable::colformat_double(j = c("Ratio", "SE"), digits = 2) %>%
  flextable::bold(part = "header", bold = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::add_footer_lines(
    values = c(
      "Note 1: Tukey-adjusted wald tests performed on the log scale, based on the asymptotic distribution of the estimates.",
      "Note 2: P-values < 0.05 indicate that the predicted number of 30-day UHRs at the contrasted time points were significantly different."
    )
  ) %>%
  flextable::font(part = "all", fontname = "Century Gothic") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "all", size = 11) %>%
  flextable::italic(part = "footer", italic = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::align(part = "footer", align = "left") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "footer", size = 9)  

tbl_contrast_nb_full_model_int_same_day
```

```{r}
readmissions_by_age_int_same_day_sr <- emmeans(

  flextable::flextable() %>%
  # second header row (default) labels

    colwidths = c(1, 2)
  ) %>%

  values = c(
    "Note 1: the endpoint was scaled to 100 index admissions as standard practice to facilitate interpretation.",
    "Note 2: results indicate, at each age, the expected number of 30-day unplanned readmissions per 100 index admissions (or 100 discharges), shown separately for seizure-related and non–seizure-related index admissions."
  )) %>%

  flextable::align(j = 2:3, part = "body", align = "center")
```

###### Contrast between time points of interest

```{r}
#| label: tbl-contrast-time-points-model-nb-int-sr-same-day
#| tbl-cap: "Pairwise contrast for time-points of interest (6, 12, 18, and 24 months) with interaction term"
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| results: 'markup'

# obtain time point of interest to compare from the total emmeans grid
emm_subset_nb_model_int_same_day_sr <- subset(readmissions_by_age_int_same_day_sr, 
                                   age_index_admission_yr %in% c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2))

# time point comparison
contrast_nb_model_int_same_day_sr <- emmeans::contrast(
  emm_subset_nb_model_int_same_day_sr,
  method = "pairwise", 
  # reference is 0.5 years
  ref = 1,
  # keeps comparisons within each level
  by = "seizure_related_index_admission",
  adjust = "tukey") 

tbl_contrast_nb_model_int_same_day_sr <- contrast_nb_model_int_same_day_sr %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  transmute(
    # Clean the contrast labels from the age term and make it "a vs b"
    `Contrasted time-points (years)` =
      str_squish(str_replace_all(contrast, c("age_index_admission_yr" = "", "/" = " vs "))),
    `Type of admission diagnosis` = factor(
      seizure_related_index_admission,
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c("Non-seizure-related", "Seizure-related")),
    Ratio = ratio,
    SE = SE,
    `P value` = case_when(
      p.value < 1e-4 ~ "< 0.0001",
      p.value < 0.05 ~ "< 0.05",
      TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", p.value)
    )
  ) %>%
  flextable::regulartable() %>%
  flextable::colformat_double(j = c("Ratio", "SE") , digits = 2) %>%
  flextable::autofit() %>%
  flextable::add_footer_lines(
    values = c(
      "Note 1: Tukey-adjusted wald tests performed on the log scale, based on the asymptotic distribution of the estimates.",
      "Note 2: P-values < 0.05 indicate that the predicted number of 30-day UHRs at the contrasted time points were significantly different."
    )
  ) %>%
  flextable::font(part = "all", fontname = "Century Gothic") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "all", size = 11) %>%
  flextable::italic(part = "footer", italic = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::align(part = "footer", align = "left") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "footer", size = 9) %>%
  flextable::bold(part = "header", bold = TRUE)
  
tbl_contrast_nb_model_int_same_day_sr
```
