## Sensitivity analysis (II): Merging hospital admission records occurring on the day after last discharge

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}

```{r}
#| label: sensitivity-analyses-merging-admissions-next-day-rename
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

# Select, order and rename variables for readmission df
#' Note: readmission variable used to filter the desired subset of data
#' was derived in the data management file
readmissions_merged_next_day_df <- hospitalizations_merged_next_day_df %>%
  #' keep index with valid exptime and remove those with invalid index 
  #' admission which doens't allow to count readmissions (i.e. exptime == 0)
  #' Index derived in the data management file already excludes planned, birth
  #'  and outpatient admissions
  filter(readmission == "index" & !is.na(count_readmissions)) %>%
  # order, rename and select variables of interest
  dplyr::select(
    # patient identifier
    patient_uuid,
    # admissions related features
    admission_age_days_firstDate,
    admission_age_days_lastDate,
    # demographics
    sex,
    age_index_admission_yr = age_admission_yr,
    # genetic mutations
    other_epilepsy_mutations,
    recurrent_variant,
    neonatal_onset,
    # clinical history
    seizure_related_index_admission = seizure_related_admission,
    length_of_index_stay_days_cat = length_of_stay_days_cat,
    respiratory_support_index_admission = respiratory_support_admission,
    tech_assistance_ever,
    count_readmissions,
    exptime,
    # treatment history
    vns_insertion_ever,
    n_distinct_asm_index_admission = n_distinct_asm_admission,
    adverse_effect_index_admission = adverse_effect_admission,
    ketogenic_diet_admission,
    quinidine_admission
    )
```

```{r}
#| label: sensitivity-analyses-merging-admissions-model-next-day
#| echo: false

nb_model_sensit_df_next_day <- readmissions_merged_next_day_df %>%
  # select variables of interest
  dplyr::select(
    - admission_age_days_firstDate,
    - admission_age_days_lastDate
  ) %>%
  # drop levels to remove those with no observations
  droplevels() 
```

```{r}
#| label: sensitivity-analyses-merging-admissions-model-next-day-structure
#| echo: false
#| results: false

str(nb_model_sensit_df_next_day)
```

### NB minimal - Linear age (RI + RS)

Pre and post modelling assumptions were checked (see [appendix](#appendix)).

```{r}
#| label: model-next-day-nb-minimal
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'

#' it couldn't converge with the RS even with control arguments added
nb_model_min_sensit_next_day <- glmmTMB(
  count_readmissions ~
    age_index_admission_yr +             
    offset(log(exptime)) + 
    (1 + age_index_admission_yr | patient_uuid),
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = nb_model_sensit_df_next_day
)

summary(nb_model_min_sensit_next_day)
```

```{r}
#| label: model-next-day-nb-minimal-ri-only
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'

#' it couldn't converge with the RS even with control arguments added
nb_model_min_sensit_only_ri_next_day <- glmmTMB(
  count_readmissions ~
    age_index_admission_yr +             
    offset(log(exptime)) + 
    (1 | patient_uuid), # random slope was removed
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = nb_model_sensit_df_next_day
)

summary(nb_model_min_sensit_only_ri_next_day)
```

### NB minimal model - Non-lineal structural form of time (RCS)

```{r}
#| label: nb-rcs-minimal-test-optimal-knots-sensit-next-day
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'
#| message: false
#| warning: false

optimal_knots_next_day <- suppressMessages(
  test_knots_ns_glmmTMB(
    data = nb_model_sensit_df_next_day,
    predictor = "age_index_admission_yr",
    response = "count_readmissions",
    fixed_effects = NULL, # without covariates
    random_effect = "1 | patient_uuid",
    offset_var = "exptime",
    k_vec = c(3,4,5),
    family = nbinom2(link = "log")
  )
)

optimal_knots_next_day
```

The optimal number of knots for the sensitivity analyses population with merged admissions on the next day of discharge was 3, as it had the lowest AIC value. Similar results were obtained when tested the optimal number with all covariates.

```{r}
#| label: number_knots-sensit-next-day
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'
#| message: false
#| warning: false

#' Defining knots for RCS:
#' default position of knots based on quantiles 25%, 50% and 75%
knots_rcs_next_day <- attributes(rcs(
  nb_model_sensit_df_next_day$age_index_admission_yr, 3))$parms

# display knots location for age at index admission
paste0("Knots for age at index admission (years): ",
       paste(round(knots_rcs_next_day, 2), collapse = ", "))
```

```{r}
#| label: model-next-day-nb-rcs-full
#| echo: false

# fit the stepwise model with merged admissions for same day of discharge
nb_model_rcs_min_sensit_next_day <- glmmTMB(
  count_readmissions ~ 
    ns(age_index_admission_yr, 
        knots = knots_rcs_next_day[2], # internal knot
        Boundary.knots = c(knots_rcs_next_day[1], knots_rcs_next_day[3])) + # boundary knots
    offset(log(exptime)) + 
    (1 | patient_uuid),
  data = nb_model_sensit_df_next_day,
  family = nbinom2(link = "log")
  )

summary(nb_model_rcs_min_sensit_next_day)
```

### Comparing performance of minimal models

```{r}
#| label: tbl-nb-performance-comparison-minimal-sensit-next-day
#| tbl-cap: "Comparing performance of minimal models based on differernt performance indices"
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'

compare_performance(nb_model_min_sensit_next_day, # with random slope and intercept
                    nb_model_min_sensit_only_ri_next_day, # only random intercept
                    nb_model_rcs_min_sensit_next_day) # with restricted cubic splines
```

The model with RCS improved the model fit compared to the minimal model without RCS (@tbl-nb-performance-comparison-minimal-sensit-next-day) and it has satisfied the modelling assumptions (see [appendix](#appendix)). Therefore, the model with RCS was used as basis for further analysis.

### Covariate selection

The same set of covariates as in the main analyses were considered for this sensitivity analyses.

##### Automatic stepwise selection

```{r}
#| label: nb-main-model-stepwise-automatic-sensit-next-day
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false
#| message: false

stepwise_backward_test_next_day <- buildmer::buildglmmTMB(
  #' formula mentioned in the main analyses
  f, 
  data = nb_model_sensit_df_next_day,
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  buildmerControl = buildmerControl(
    # forced terms
    include = ~ ns(age_index_admission_yr, 
                   knots = knots_rcs_next_day[2],
                   Boundary.knots = c(knots_rcs_next_day[1],
                                      knots_rcs_next_day[3])) +
      sex + offset(log(exptime)) + (1 | patient_uuid),
    #' order step to reach first the maximal feasible model and then eliminate
    #'  terms in backward direction
    direction = c('order', 'backward'), 
    #' Criterion used to test terms for their contribution to the model fit
    crit = 'AIC',
    #' Criterion used to test terms for elimination in the elimination step
    elim = 'AIC',
    #' glmmTMB's control here to pass the lack of convergence when adding 
    #' sex to the minimal
    args = list(control = glmmTMBControl(
      optimizer = optim,
      optArgs = list(method = "BFGS")
    ))
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: nb-main-model-stepwise-automatic-sensit-next-day-print-formula
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| results: 'markup'
#| message: false

# note: the output was saved in r rds file as takes time to run
# dir.create("~/RWE-rare_disease/Hospitalizations/output/rds_data")
#saveRDS(stepwise_backward_test_next_day, "rds_data/stepwise_backward_test_next_day.rds")

# Load the saved stepwise backward test file
stepwise_backward_test_next_day_file <- readRDS("rds_data/stepwise_backward_test_next_day.rds")

# assign the formula from the stepwise backward test
automatic_backward_stepwise_next_day <- formula(stepwise_backward_test_next_day_file@model)

# print the formula
automatic_backward_stepwise_next_day
```

The automatic backward stepwise selection procedure removed six covariates from the maximal feasible model: `vns_insertion_ever`, `tech_assistance_ever`, `neonatal_onset`, `adverse_effect_index_admission`, `quinidine_admission` and `ketogenic_diet_admission`.

```{r}
#| label: nb-rcs-stepwise-automatic-selection-next-day
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'

nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_next_day <- glmmTMB(
  # formula from the automatic stepwise selection
  formula = automatic_backward_stepwise_next_day,
  data = nb_model_sensit_df_next_day,
  family = nbinom2(link = "log")
)

summary(nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_next_day)
```

The robustness of the stepwise selection results was further evaluated through model averaging across all possible covariate combinations (see [appendix](#appendix)).This assessment confirmed the stepwise model (`nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_next_day`) as the an appropriate **main effects model** for subsequent analyses.

The final retained covariates were: `sex`, `age_index_admission_yr`, `other_epilepsy_mutations`, `recurrent_variant`, `length_of_index_stay_days_cat`, `respiratory_support_index_admission`, `n_distinct_asm_index_admission` and `seizure_related_index_admission`.

### Testing inteaction terms

The interaction terms were added one by one to the main effects model obtained in the previous step, and the goodness of fit was assessed using AIC and the LRT to compare the model without interaction terms as performed for the main analyses.

#### Age at index admission with sex

```{r}
#| label: interaction-terms-sex-age-next-day
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'
#| warning: false

nb_model_rcs_int_sex_age_next_day <- glmmTMB(
  count_readmissions ~ 
    offset(log(exptime)) +
    ns(age_index_admission_yr,  
       knots = knots_rcs_next_day[2], 
       Boundary.knots = c(knots_rcs_next_day[1], 
                          knots_rcs_next_day[3]))*sex +
    length_of_index_stay_days_cat +  
    other_epilepsy_mutations + 
    recurrent_variant + 
    respiratory_support_index_admission +  
    seizure_related_index_admission +
    n_distinct_asm_index_admission +
    (1 | patient_uuid),
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = nb_model_sensit_df_next_day
)

# the interaction does not significantly improves the goodness of fit of the model.
anova(nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_next_day, nb_model_rcs_int_sex_age_next_day)
```

#### Age at index admission with seizure-related index admission

```{r}

  count_readmissions ~ 
    offset(log(exptime)) +

       knots = knots_rcs_next_day[2],

                          knots_rcs_next_day[3]))*seizure_related_index_admission +

))

anova(nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_next_day , nb_model_rcs_int_age_sr_next_day) 
```

#### Age at index admission with number of ASMs at index admission

```{r}
#| label: interaction-terms-age-asm-next-day
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'

nb_model_rcs_int_age_asm_next_day <- glmmTMB(
  count_readmissions ~ 
    offset(log(exptime)) +
    ns(age_index_admission_yr,  
       knots = knots_rcs_next_day[2], 
       Boundary.knots = c(knots_rcs_next_day[1], 
                          knots_rcs_next_day[3]))*n_distinct_asm_index_admission +
    sex +
    length_of_index_stay_days_cat + 
    other_epilepsy_mutations + 
    recurrent_variant +
    respiratory_support_index_admission +  
    seizure_related_index_admission +
    (1 | patient_uuid),
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = nb_model_sensit_df_next_day,
  control = glmmTMBControl(
    optimizer = optim, 
    optArgs = list(method = "BFGS")
))

# the interaction significantly improves the goodness of fit of the model (0.005633 **).
anova(nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_next_day, nb_model_rcs_int_age_asm_next_day) 
```

Two interactions significantly (p \< 0.05) improved the goodness of fit of the model: the interaction between the interaction between `age_index_admission_yr` with `n_distinct_asm_index_admission`.

Although the `age_admission_yr` x `number of ASMs at index admission` was statistically significant by LRT, the observed differences occurred mainly at older ages where very few patients were available for comparison. This resulted in unstable estimates with wide confidence intervals, limiting the reliability of the effect.

Thus the **preliminary final model** and **final model** was the main effects model without interaction terms `nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_next_day`.

The final model has converged properly and satisfied the model assumptions (see [appendix](#appendix)).

:::

      "Estimates are adjusted for all variables in the model. Nonlinear spline terms and random-effect estimates are not reported.",
      sep = " "
    )

#### Marginal means estimations

##### Main effect of age at index admission

###### Table: predicted 30-day UHR across age at index admission

```{r}
#| label: tbl-emmeans-table-sensit-next-day
#| tbl-cap: "Overall estimated marginal means of the number of 30-day UHR per 100 index admissions"
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'
#| warning: false

# Build the reference grid explicitly
grid_emmeans_full_next_day <- ref_grid(
  nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_next_day,
  at = list(age_index_admission_yr = age_seq), # age seq as defined in main analyses
  non.nuisance = "age_index_admission_yr", # do not average
  params = "knots_rcs_next_day",  # state knot values for the splines model
  weights = "equal" # assume equal weights for the emmeans
)

# Define total standard deviation for bias adjustment (only random is given)
cor_random_mod_next_day <- lme4::VarCorr(
  nb_model_rcs_stepwise_sensit_next_day)
total_sd_next_day <- sapply(cor_random_mod_next_day$cond, function(x) attr(x, "stddev"))

#' Model with offset, weights assumed equal
readmissions_by_age_next_day <- emmeans(
  grid_emmeans_full_next_day, ~ age_index_admission_yr,
  type = "response",  
  offset = mean(log(nb_model_sensit_df_next_day$exptime)),
  bias.adjust = TRUE,
  sigma = total_sd_next_day
  )

# Convert the emmeans object to a regular dataframe
readmissions_by_age_next_day_df <- as.data.frame(readmissions_by_age_next_day)

# View the updated dataframe
tbl_readmissions_by_age_next_day_df <- readmissions_by_age_next_day_df %>%
  mutate(
    combined = sprintf(
      "%.1f (%.1f; %.1f)",
      # Scaling up the number per 100 index with respective IC95%
      response * 100, asymp.LCL * 100, asymp.UCL * 100
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(age_index_admission_yr, combined) %>%
  rename(
    "Age at index admission (years)" = age_index_admission_yr,
    "Number of 30-day UHRs per 100 index admissions (95% CI)" = combined
  ) %>%
  flextable::regulartable() %>%
  flextable::autofit() %>%
  flextable::bold(part = "header", bold = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::add_footer_lines(values = c(
    "Note 1: the endpoint was scaled to 100 index admissions as standard practice to facilitate interpretation.",
    "Note 2: results indicate, at each age, how many 30-day unplanned readmissions would be expected for every 100 index admissions (or 100 discharges)."
  )) %>%
  flextable::font(part = "all", fontname = "Century Gothic") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "all", size = 11) %>%
  flextable::italic(part = "footer", italic = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::align(part = "footer", align = "left") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "footer", size = 9) %>%
  flextable::align(j = 1, part = "all", align = "left") %>%
  flextable::align(j = 2, part = "all", align = "center")

tbl_readmissions_by_age_next_day_df
```

###### Contrast for time-points of interest

```{r}
#| label: tbl-contrast-time-points-model-nb-int-next-day
#| tbl-cap: "Pairwise contrast for time-points of interest (6, 12, 18, and 24 months)"
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| results: 'markup'

# obtain time point of interest to compare from the total emmeans grid
emm_subset_nb_model_next_day <- subset(readmissions_by_age_next_day, 
                                   age_index_admission_yr %in% c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2))

# time point comparison
contrast_nb_model_int_next_day <- emmeans::contrast(emm_subset_nb_model_next_day,
                                            method = "pairwise", 
                                            ref = 1, # reference is 0.5 years
                                            adjust = "tukey"
                                            ) 

tbl_contrast_nb_model_int_next_day <- contrast_nb_model_int_next_day %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::select(-c("df", "null", "z.ratio")) %>%
  transmute(
    `Contrasted time-points (years)` =
      str_squish(str_replace_all(contrast, c("age_index_admission_yr" = "", "/" = " vs "))),
    Ratio = ratio,
    SE = SE,
    `P value` = case_when(
      p.value < 1e-4 ~ "< 0.0001",
      p.value < 0.05 ~ "< 0.05",
      TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", p.value)
    )
  ) %>%
  flextable::regulartable() %>%
  flextable::autofit() %>%
  flextable::colformat_double(j = c("Ratio", "SE"), digits = 2) %>%
  flextable::bold(part = "header", bold = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::add_footer_lines(
    values = c(
      "Note 1: Tukey-adjusted wald tests performed on the log scale, based on the asymptotic distribution of the estimates.",
      "Note 2: P-values < 0.05 indicate that the predicted number of 30-day UHRs at the contrasted time points were significantly different."
    )
  ) %>%
  flextable::font(part = "all", fontname = "Century Gothic") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "all", size = 11) %>%
  flextable::italic(part = "footer", italic = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::align(part = "footer", align = "left") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "footer", size = 9)  

tbl_contrast_nb_model_int_next_day
```

# Appendix {#appendix}

## Data layout

In this example for few patients, each row corresponds to one index admission. The variable `count_readmissions` corresponds to the number of 30-day UHRs occurring after each index admission. The variable `exptime` corresponds to the exposure time in days for each index admission, which is used as an offset in the NB model. The variable `patient_seq_id` is a numeric identifier for each patient, which is used as a random effect in the NB model to account for multiple index admissions per patient. The age at index admission is represented by the variable `age_index_admission_yr` in years, is used as main timescale in the models and the rest of variables are the covariates included in the models. Some of them are fixed over time (e.g., `sex`) while others are time-varying covariates (e.g., `seizure_related_index_admission`).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-readmissions-layout-main-df
#| tbl-cap: "Data layout for 30-day UHR endpoint for 5 patients ('patient_seq_id') with three covariates. Each observation corresponds to one index admission"
#| echo: false

#| warning: false

readmissions_df_layout <- readmissions_df %>%
  # replace original patient_uuid ids to display data
  mutate(patient_seq_id = as.numeric(factor(patient_uuid))) %>%
  arrange(patient_seq_id, age_index_admission_yr) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    patient_seq_id, 
    sex,
    age_index_admission_yr,
    seizure_related_index_admission
  ) %>%
  head(18) %>%                     # take first 18 rows
  flextable() %>%                  # NOW create the flextable
  autofit() %>%
  set_table_properties(width = 1, layout = "autofit") %>%  # fit page width in Word
  font(part = "all", fontname = "Century Gothic") %>%
  fontsize(part = "all", size = 11) %>%
  add_footer_lines(values = "Note: Only the first 18 rows are shown for illustrative purposes.") %>%
  fontsize(part = "footer", size = 9) %>%
  italic(part = "footer", italic = TRUE) %>%
  align(part = "footer", align = "left")

## Verification of pre-post modelling assumptions

**Pre-modelling assumptions** for negative binomial models were evaluated following the list proposed by @hilbeNegativeBinomialRegression2011 for main and sensitivity analysis:

1.  *Zero counts are possible in the outcome* Index admissions can have 0 count of 30-day UHRs.

2.  *Excess zeros in the outcome (more than than NB model accounts for)*. This violation was checked due to the high proportion of zeros (\~60% of index admission have no subsequent 30-day UHR event.

Although it has been argued that NB models can adequately handle excess zeros [@fernandezComparisonStatisticalMethods2022], it was formally assessed this assumption by comparing observed and predicted zeros using `performance` package. For each analysis, the ratio of observed to predicted zeros was within the predefined tolerance range.

There was no indication of zero-inflation, and a ZINB model was not required as the proposed negative binomial model adequately captured the excess zero.

3.  *When zeros and positives values are assumed to be separated by an obstacle (hurdle or threshold), a hurdle model may be better.* This assumption does not apply here, the count of UHRs (0,1,2,3…) comes from the same underlying process (readmissions per index admission).

4.  *Censoring.* Accounted by using the actual observed follow-up time ≤30 days as offset term. Moreover, records with no at-risk time or in-hospital death were excluded, as they cannot experience the outcome.

5.  *Truncation (counts below or above threshold are excluded).* Zeros are included, and all counts ≥0 are recorded.

6.  *Within-subject correlation*. It was accounted with the use of both random intercept and random slope.

7.  *Selection mechanism (when counts only occur if another variable passes a threshold*. There is no indication our data has a selection mechanism.

8.  *Endogeneity (omitted variables / mismeasurement / categorization bias affecting predictors)*. It was accounted accounted by through careful covariate selection and planned sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results for 30-day UHRs

Lastly, for **post-modelling assumptions**, overdispersion, collinearity (in body document), normality of random effects (QQ plot and normality test) and the linearity of the effect of age at index admission (main timescale) were checked:

1.  *Overdispersion*. No overdispersion was detected in any of the minimal models.

2.  *Collinearity*. It was low (VIF \< 3) in all maximal feasibles and final models. It is important to mention that VIF values for variables algebraically connected to each other such as the restricted cubic splines should not be interpreted [@harrellRegressionModelingStrategies2015].

3.  *Normality of random effects*. Normality tests indicated some deviation from normality of random slopes and random intercept in sensitivity analysis. However, QQ plots showed that random effects followed the expected normal quantiles closely, with only mild tail deviations.

4.  *Linearity of the log-link function for age at index admission*. It was evaluated through residuals vs. fitted plots and by comparing the fit of models with age entered as a linear term versus restricted cubic splines. Models with splines consistently showed improved fit as described for each of the analysis.

res_df_next_day <- data.frame(
  age   = nb_model_sensit_df_next_day$age_index_admission_yr,
  resid = resid(nb_model_min_sensit_next_day, type = "pearson")
)

plot(res_df_next_day$age, res_df_next_day$resid, pch = 16, col = "blue",
     xlab = "Age at index admission (years)", ylab = "Pearson residuals")
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
lines(lowess(res_df_next_day$age, res_df_next_day$resid, f = 0.8))
```

## Model averaging and all combinations

### Main analyses

```{r}
#| label: all-model-combinations-from-maximal-feasible-model
#| echo: false
#| eval: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# set max feasible/full model with RCS and all covariates
nb_model_rcs_max_feasible <- glmmTMB(
  count_readmissions ~
    ns(age_index_admission_yr,
      knots = knots_rcs[2:3],
      Boundary.knots = c(knots_rcs[1], knots_rcs[4])
    ) + sex + offset(log(exptime)) +
    neonatal_onset +
    other_epilepsy_mutations +
    recurrent_variant +
    seizure_related_index_admission +
    length_of_index_stay_days_cat +
    respiratory_support_index_admission +
    tech_assistance_ever +
    vns_insertion_ever +
    n_distinct_asm_index_admission +
    adverse_effect_index_admission +
    ketogenic_diet_admission +
    quinidine_admission +
    (1 | patient_uuid),
  data = nb_model_main_df,
  family = nbinom2()
)

#' Dredge exhaustively fits all possible combinations of fixed effects:
#'  https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/MuMIn/MuMIn.pdf
#'  https://uoftcoders.github.io/rcourse/lec09-model-selection.html#step_1:_create_saturated_model

options(na.action = "na.fail") # Required by dredge

model_all_combinations <- dredge(
  # start from maximal feasible model
  nb_model_rcs_max_feasible, 
  trace = 2, # show progress bar 
  # terms to force (random effects are already accounted)
  fixed = c(
    "cond(sex)",
    "cond(ns(age_index_admission_yr, 
       knots = knots_rcs[2:3], 
       Boundary.knots = c(knots_rcs[1], knots_rcs[4])))",
    "cond(offset(log(exptime)))"),
  # criteria to rank models
  rank = "AIC")

options(na.action = "na.omit") # set back to default
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-all-model-combinations-from-maximal-feasible-model-2
#| tbl-cap: "All model combinations from the maximal feasible model"
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: 'markup'

# note: the output was saved in r rds file as takes close to 2 hs to run
# dir.create("~/RWE-rare_disease/Hospitalizations/output/rds_data")
#saveRDS(model_all_combinations, "rds_data/model_all_combinations_new.rds")

# If already saved, just load it
model_all_combinations_full <- readRDS("rds_data/model_all_combinations_new.rds")

# view first rows of the model combinations
head(model_all_combinations_full, 10) 

# # model with the lowest AIC from all possible combinations
# lowest_aic_model <- get.models(model_all_combinations_full, subset = 1)[[1]]

# # extract formula of the model with the lowest AIC
# all_combinations_lowest_aic <- formula(lowest_aic_model)
# all_combinations_lowest_aic
```

Compared to the stepwise selection, when an exhaustive process of all possible combinations of covariates is conducted, it can be observed that among 8192 possible combinations, the model with the lowest AIC differs with the stepwise in the exclusion of `seizure_related_index_admission` and `n_distinct_asm_index_admission`. Additionally, a slightly lower AIC for the model obtained through all combinations (615.5 vs. 616.1) was observed.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-all-model-combinations-model-avg
#| tbl-cap: "Model averaging from all model combinations"
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| results: 'markup'

# 1. get list of models with an AIC value (converged models)
models_converged_list <- model_all_combinations_full[!is.na(model_all_combinations_full$AIC), ]

# 2. get models with delta AIC ≤ 2 of difference to the lowest AIC model
#' Note: models with values less than 2 are considered to be essentially
#'  as good as the best model.
# https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00265-010-1037-6
avg_mod <- model.avg(models_converged_list, subset = delta <= 2) # 39 models

# 3. Summary of the model averaging
#' Note: here it can be observed the combination of variables in the models that
#'  are separated by less than 2 units to the model with the lowest AIC
#'  From the full averaging part of the output:
#'  How much that predictor changes the model’s predicted outcome, on average
#'   across the top AIC-supported models, after accounting for model selection
#'    uncertainty.
summary(avg_mod)

# Sum of model weights over all models including each variable.
#' https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7855182/
#' https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00265-010-1037-6
#' Note1: If a particular variable appears in all models, then its summed Akaike 
#' weight will tend towards 1. otherwise its weight will tend  towards 0.
#' Note2: Some authors may put a 0.9 or 0.95 to define the threshold of 
#' importance, but it is not a strict rule. 
#' Indicates how often and with what support each variable appears in the set of models.
sw(avg_mod) # sum of weights
```

When obtaining the list of models with a delta AIC ≤ 2 from the model with the lowest AIC (39 models), it can be observed that the covariate `length_of_index_stay_days_cat` and `adverse_effect_index_admission` were present in all models (sum of weights = 1) besides the forced ones (age, sex and offset). Among the other variables, `recurrent_variant` (0.93) and `quinidine_admission` (0.80) showed high importance, being present in 36 and 30 models, respectively.

The covariates `other_epilepsy_mutations` (0.69), `ketogenic_diet_admission` (0.61), `seizure_related_index_admission` (0.47) and `respiratory_support_index_admission` (0.38), had moderate weights, appearing in 16–27 models within the delta AIC ≤ 2 set. Interestingly, `n_distinct_asm_index_admission` (0.24) was retained in the stepwise model, despite having a lower weight than `respiratory_support_index_admission` (0.38), which was excluded in the final step.

Finally, `tech_assistance_ever` (0.22), `vns_insertion_ever` (0.04), and `neonatal_onset` (0.04) had very low weights with presence in 2-10 out of 39 models, confirming their limited contribution to model fit.

*Note: Because `respiratory_support_index_admission` was excluded while `n_distinct_asm_index_admission` was retained in the stepwise model. Despite the opposite pattern observed for those two covariates in the model averaging analysis, the stepwise and maximum feasible model procedures were also re-estimated with alternative optimizer settings, yielding identical results to the default estimation.*

# Complementary analyses

## Distribution of index admissions by count of 30-day UHR events.
```{r}
#| label: tbl-descriptive-index-number-by-count-30-day-uhr-events
#| tbl-cap: "Distribution of index admissions by count of 30-day UHR events"
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'

# patient-level summary count of max uhr
 patient_unique_counts <- readmissions_df %>%
   group_by(patient_uuid) %>%
   summarise(
     count_readmissions = max(count_readmissions),
     .groups = "drop"
   )
 patient_summary <- patient_unique_counts %>%
   group_by(count_readmissions) %>%
   summarise(
     n_patients = n(),
     prop_patients = n() / n_distinct(readmissions_df$patient_uuid) * 100,
     .groups = "drop"
   )
 # admission-level summary
 admission_summary <- readmissions_df %>%
   group_by(count_readmissions) %>%
   summarise(
     n_admissions = n(),
     prop_admissions = n() / nrow(readmissions_df) * 100,
     .groups = "drop"
   )
 # join both tables
 combined_summary <- full_join(patient_summary,
   admission_summary,
   by = "count_readmissions"
 ) %>%
   arrange(count_readmissions)
 
 # Rename the count_readmissions column for clarity
summary_per_index <- combined_summary %>%
  mutate(
    count_and_prop = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n_admissions, round(prop_admissions, 1))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    `Count of UHR per index admission` = count_readmissions,
    `Number of index admissions` = count_and_prop
  )


summary_per_index %>%
  flextable::regulartable() %>%
  flextable::autofit() %>%
  flextable::bold(part = "header", bold = TRUE) %>%  
  flextable::add_footer_lines(
    values = c(
      "Note: Percentage relative to total number of index admissions (N = 365)."
    )
  )  %>%
  flextable::font(part = "all", fontname = "Century Gothic") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "all", size = 11) %>%
  flextable::italic(part = "footer", italic = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::align(part = "footer", align = "left") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "footer", size = 9) 
```

## Number of 30-day UHR per index admission over follow-up
```{r}
#| label: tbl-descriptive-number-of-30-day-uhr-events-per-index-admission
#| tbl-cap: "Number of 30-day UHR per index admission over follow-up"
#| echo: false
#| results: 'markup'


# total 30-day UHRs for each patient over follow up
uhr_by_patient <- readmissions_df %>%
  group_by(patient_uuid) %>%
  summarise(
    # sum of 30-day UHRs per patient during follow-up
    patient_readmissions = mean(count_readmissions, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# summary across patients
uhr_by_across_patient <- uhr_by_patient %>%
  summarise(
    # mean (average) number of UHRs per patient
    mean_uhr = mean(patient_readmissions, na.rm = TRUE),
    # standard deviation of UHRs per patient
    sd_uhr = sd(patient_readmissions),
    # median (50th percentile) number of UHRs per patient
    median_uhr = median(patient_readmissions),
    # minimum number of UHRs observed
    min_uhr = min(patient_readmissions),
    # maximum number of UHRs observed
    max_uhr = max(patient_readmissions),
    # 25th percentile (Q1) of UHRs per patient
    q25_uhr = quantile(patient_readmissions, 0.25),
    # 75th percentile (Q3) of UHRs per patient
    q75_uhr = quantile(patient_readmissions, 0.75)
  )

uhr_summary_table <- tibble(
  'Summary statistic' = c(
    "Mean UHRs (SD)",
    "Median UHRs (Q1–Q3)",
    "Range UHRs (min–max)"
  ),
  'Number of 30-day UHRs per index' = c(
    sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", uhr_by_across_patient$mean_uhr, uhr_by_across_patient$sd_uhr),
    sprintf("%.1f (%.1f–%.1f)", uhr_by_across_patient$median_uhr, uhr_by_across_patient$q25_uhr, uhr_by_across_patient$q75_uhr),
    sprintf("%.1f–%.1f", uhr_by_across_patient$min_uhr, uhr_by_across_patient$max_uhr)
  )
)

uhr_summary_table %>%
  flextable::regulartable() %>%
  flextable::autofit() %>% 
  flextable::bold(part = "header", bold = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::add_footer_lines(
    values = c(
      "Note: Patient's UHRs was first summarized by the mean/median for each patient. Patient-level values were
then used to compute the overall mean (SD) and median (Q1–Q3)/(Min–Max) during the study
period for all patients."
    )
  )  %>%
  flextable::font(part = "all", fontname = "Century Gothic") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "all", size = 11) %>%
  flextable::italic(part = "footer", italic = TRUE) %>%
  flextable::align(part = "footer", align = "left") %>%
  flextable::fontsize(part = "footer", size = 9)
```
